supported_statement: Short-term adult ADHD CBT benefit is possible; certainty and comparison matter.
checked_material: Cochrane systematic review; abstract and bibliographic metadata checked.
scope_limit: Not proof of universal benefit, long-term effectiveness or executive-function moderation.

supported_statement: CBT outperformed relaxation with educational support in medication-treated adults with persistent ADHD symptoms.
checked_material: Randomized adult ADHD trial; abstract and metadata checked.
scope_limit: Do not generalize to unmedicated populations or isolate cognitive restructuring.

supported_statement: Pretreatment flexibility did not predict overall outcome; associations with restructuring-related measures were mixed.
checked_material: Pilot older-adult anxiety/depression study; abstract and metadata checked.
scope_limit: Not adult ADHD or a direct randomized ADHD treatment-effect moderator test.

supported_statement: Pilot research relates executive functioning to CBT response in anxious older adults.
checked_material: Pilot older-adult anxiety study; abstract and metadata checked.
scope_limit: Classification uses pre/post executive functioning; not a pure baseline ADHD moderator result.

supported_statement: Moderation concerns differential treatment effects; prediction and mediation are different questions.
checked_material: Methods paper; abstract and metadata checked.
scope_limit: Conceptual framework, not clinical evidence about CBT efficacy.

checked_material: Primary reporting-guideline paper; published page and metadata checked.
scope_limit: Following a planned checklist is not completed screening or proof of review quality.

supported_statement: AMSTAR 2 is a critical appraisal tool for systematic reviews.
checked_material: Primary tool paper; bibliographic identity/title checked.
scope_limit: Tool choice only; no appraisal ratings have been made.

checked_material: Primary guideline paper; abstract and metadata checked.
scope_limit: No claim all databases have been searched.

supported_statement: A recent meta-analysis includes executive-function outcomes after adult ADHD CBT.
checked_material: Adult ADHD meta-analysis; abstract and metadata checked.
scope_limit: Executive function as an outcome does not establish baseline moderation.

supported_statement: A recent synthesis examines functioning and quality of life and reports design and bias limitations.
checked_material: Adult ADHD meta-analysis; abstract and metadata checked.
scope_limit: Includes multiple designs; no pooled effect is independently reproduced here.

supported_statement: Placebo-controlled anxiety trials support benefit; completer analyses and comparator definitions affect interpretation.
checked_material: Abstract and bibliographic metadata; clinical efficacy synthesis.
scope_limit: Package benefit does not identify restructuring as the active ingredient; no universal failure claim.

supported_statement: CBT benefits depression relative to controls; superiority over other psychotherapies is small and not robust across sensitivity analyses.
checked_material: Abstract and bibliographic metadata; comparative depression meta-analysis.
scope_limit: No proof of equivalence or superiority of mindfulness; includes several ages and settings.

supported_statement: Across adult conditions CBT effects depend on controls; study quality, heterogeneity and long-term follow-up limit interpretation.
checked_material: Publisher main text, abstract and metadata; cross-condition synthesis.
scope_limit: Inactive-control comparisons do not establish superiority to other effective therapies; no new pooling here.

supported_statement: Anxiety response rates vary with definition and analysis population; substantial nonresponse remains.
checked_material: Abstract and bibliographic metadata; systematic review of response definitions.
scope_limit: Response is not remission; do not reinterpret nonresponse as deterioration or a causal treatment failure rate.

supported_statement: A depression component trial did not identify better outcomes from full cognitive therapy than component treatments.
checked_material: Abstract and bibliographic metadata; randomized component trial.
scope_limit: A nonsignificant difference is not proof of equivalence or universal dispensability of restructuring.

supported_statement: Stress can impair prefrontal cognitive functioning, motivating an executive-demand hypothesis.
checked_material: Abstract and bibliographic metadata; mechanistic review.
scope_limit: Not a CBT trial or direct evidence of clinical moderation; impaired does not mean permanently unavailable.
